question.text: Two long parallel wires carrying currents <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> in opposite directions are placed at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from each other. A point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is at equidistant from both the wires such that the lines joining the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> to the wires are perpendicular to each other. The magnitude of magnetic field at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. (Given: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn></math>)

solution.text:
Here, the magnetic fields produced by the two wires will be perpendicular to one another.

Magnetic field due to wire carrying current 8 A is B1=μ0i12πd

and magnetic field due to wire carrying current 15 A is B2=μ0i22πd

The net magnetic field is 

Bnet=B12+B22=μ02πdi12+i22

=4π×10-72π×72×10-2×82+152 d=72 cm

=68×10-6  T.
